description: A corrected HSTU cold start for sequential recommendation on four Amazon categories: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Train one independent HSTU model per category and select changes using macro-average validation HR@10. The supplied content defines an experimental protocol rather than a new architecture or reported result.
motivation: Compare improvements within the HSTU family under matched data, seeds, evaluation, and compute constraints, while preventing leakage and preserving agreement between training and deployed prediction.
implementation_notes: Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Preserve the supplied splits, four-category routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep maximum epochs 200 and batches per epoch 200. For left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position rather than count-1. Each category must load exactly one trained model/checkpoint; independent-model ensembles and separately fitted score fusion are prohibited. Architecture changes must update the embedded predictor writer and family-compatible diagnosis interfaces. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and the ModelView contract. The shared search budget is 43,200 GPU-seconds. No baseline source code or measured results were supplied.
pseudocode:
set preprocessing_seed = 0
set training_seed = 42
for category in the four required categories:
    load the host-supplied fixed splits
    initialize the corrected HSTU baseline
    train one model with at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch
    use the final nonpadding history position for readout
    save one category checkpoint beneath the trial directory
write working/predict.py with matching architecture and category routing
retain family-compatible diagnostic probes
host evaluates validation HR@10 using 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and seed 42
compare candidates by macro-average validation HR@10 within the shared budget

originality.positive: Defines a carefully controlled, family-preserving evaluation setup.
originality.negative: Provides no novel HSTU mechanism, loss, or optimization method.

future_potential.positive: Supports controlled exploration of jointly trained HSTU layers, losses, sampling, and hyperparameters.
future_potential.negative: Potential gains remain unmeasured and must fit the fixed search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The host-supplied corrected baseline should provide the main training and routing structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Changes require consistent checkpoint loading, predictor generation, padding-aware readout, and diagnostic compatibility.
